consensus_findings.description: Critical: Direct registry loader `_config_from_agents_yaml` bypassed `project_principals` topology projection and validation. In commit 96827d55, `_config_from_agents_yaml` manually formatted SPIFFE IDs and passed raw `vendor_credentials` without validating against the `credential_vendors` catalog, checking for duplicate agents or slug validity, forbidding manual `openbao_role_id`, or rejecting keyless agents declaring vendor credentials. This violated the canonical principal topology contract (D1, AI-02, AI-13, AI-16). (Note: resolved in follow-up commit ad466899 via `project_principals` projection).

Keyless CLI dispatch now hard-depends on the shared openbao_credentials package. api_key_resolver.py imports it at module top, and review_dispatcher.py additionally runs `from openbao_credentials import BaoCredentialError` unconditionally inside dispatch_and_wait (line 2979), so the import executes even when every reviewer is a CLI vendor and BAO_ADDR is unset. The previous resolver imported hvac lazily inside the Bao branch and degraded gracefully. Every orchestrator skill (autopilot SKILL.md:175, iterate-on-implementation SKILL.md:482/507, parallel-review-plan SKILL.md:250, parallel-infrastructure SKILL.md:103) documents launching the dispatcher with plain `python3`, and the runtime copies under .agents/skills serve non-Claude harnesses with no skills/.venv. In this very worktree the skills venv has neither path dependency installed, so `python3 review_dispatcher.py` in pure CLI mode raises ImportError at dispatch time (the importlib fallback at lines 2940-2951 re-executes the module and propagates the same ImportError). This regresses CFG-02 (non-OpenBao profile remains compatible) and CFG-25 (CLI processes retain their existing contract). Fix: import openbao_credentials lazily inside the configured-Bao branch of resolve() and inside _resolve_dispatch_key's except clause (or catch a locally defined base), so absence of the package only matters when BAO_ADDR is set.

The SDK tier uses the pip package name (`sdk.package`) as the credential vendor id that is authorized against `vendor_credentials` and read at `vendors/<vendor>`. The registry's authorization vocabulary is the `credential_vendors` catalog (anthropic, openai, openrouter, xai). These coincide today only because the two dispatchable SDK agents use packages `anthropic` and `openai`. SdkVendorAdapter already supports `google-generativeai`, and a future xAI SDK agent would declare `vendor_credentials: [xai]` while its package would be `openai` or `xai-sdk`: the lookup would either always be denied, or an xAI request would be authorized under the `openai` scope and read the OpenAI vendor key. D1 states the catalog, not package or CLI fields, defines the vendor vocabulary. Not a blocker for the current registry, but the mapping should be explicit.

none: `ApiKeyResolver.resolve()` verifies that `principal_id` matches the canonical SPIFFE regex and checks `vendor_id in self._scopes.get(principal_id, ())` before initializing `OpenBaoClient` or calling `ensure_session` or `read_vendor_key`. Undeclared vendor credential requests fail loud with `AUTHORIZATION_DENIED` before any network or filesystem Vault access.

none: In configured OpenBao mode (`BAO_ADDR` set), `ApiKeyResolver` exclusively queries `OpenBaoClient` and raises typed `BaoCredentialError` on any error without falling back to ambient environment variables (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) or static shared-secret paths. Non-OpenBao development mode preserves configured environment key resolution.

none: SDK dispatch call site in `ReviewOrchestrator.dispatch_and_wait()` scopes credential lookup by the agent principal and declared SDK package vendor ID. When OpenBao resolution fails, error messages are sanitized (stripping backend details and secret material), mapped to `ErrorClass.AUTH`, and adapter dispatch is aborted.

none: OpenAI-compatible call site handles both metered endpoints (e.g. OpenRouter, resolved under vendor `openrouter`) and unauthenticated local endpoints (`endpoint_kind == "local"` and `principal_id is None`). Keyless local endpoints bypass Bao lookup without error, while metered endpoints fail closed with `ErrorClass.AUTH` if unauthenticated.

none: Local CLI dispatch tier preserves existing subprocess execution without invoking `ApiKeyResolver` or OpenBao credentials in pca-02, deferring credential injection to pca-04 as specified by the tier boundary.

none: `ApiKeyResolver` dropped the legacy in-memory credential cache dict (`self._cache`). Secret reads are performed afresh on each `resolve()` call via `client.read_vendor_key()`, ensuring that OpenBao key rotations take effect immediately without requiring process restart, while session token lifecycle remains serialized and protected on disk by `ensure_session()`.

In configured-Bao mode an endpoint agent without a registry `api_key` (null principal) but with an `api_key_env`, or any openrouter agent without a registry key, is sent to `resolve(None, vendor)`, which raises CONFIGURATION_INVALID with category `principal`. Failing closed is correct per D2, but the surfaced error `OpenBao credential lookup failed: CONFIGURATION_INVALID` points the operator at Bao configuration when the actual cause is that the agent has no registry principal. There is no test for the openrouter-without-principal case.

The resolver re-derives the Bao role name (`agent-<name>`) from the SPIFFE ID with a private regex and f-string (line 47) instead of using the shared topology's encoding. D1 says name encoding is centralized in the openbao_credentials package. The duplicated rule matches today (same slug pattern as topology._SLUG and adapter._PRINCIPAL) but will drift silently if the role-name encoding ever changes. Acceptable for pca-02 given the resolver only has the principal id, not the registry.

The main skill-workflow spec still requires `ApiKeyResolver` to attempt OpenBao first using the agent's `openbao_role_id` and to fall back to the environment variable. This change ships deltas only for agent-coordinator, agent-identity, and configuration, so after archive the canonical spec will contradict the implemented `resolve(principal_id, vendor_id)` contract. Outside wp-dispatch's write scope; belongs to wp-integration or an update-specs pass.

`credential_envs` is keyed by `(principal_id, vendor_id)`; two keyless SDK agents with the same package but different `api_key_env` collapse to one entry (last wins). Only affects the non-Bao development path and the current registry has no such pair, but keying by agent_id (as `credential_requests` already is) would remove the ambiguity.

The worker's claim of 180 passing tests could not be independently reproduced: the sandbox denied the pytest invocation, and this worktree's skills/.venv has neither `openbao_credentials` nor `system_one_decisions` installed under site-packages although both are declared as path dependencies in skills/pyproject.toml and uv.lock. The package verification command as written would fail with ImportError in this worktree until `uv sync` is run in skills/. The orchestrator should re-run the verification step after syncing before accepting the evidence key `dispatch_tests_passed`.

Optional: CFG-25 requires CLI dispatch to retain ambient credentials and never treat a Bao miss as a reason to switch SDK traffic to env keys. The CLI branch correctly skips ApiKeyResolver, but the wp-dispatch suite has no assertion that a CLI-tier dispatch with BAO_ADDR set leaves ApiKeyResolver.resolve uncalled.

FYI: from_config_dict uses sdk["package"] as the resolve() vendor_id for SDK tiers while OpenAI-compatible tiers hard-code openrouter|local. Current agents.yaml aligns package names with credential_vendors, so authz fails closed on mismatch, but the SDK path couples the Python package field to the D1 credential-vendor vocabulary without an explicit mapping.

Nit: OpenAI-compatible dispatch fails only when lookup_error is set, then still calls openai_adapter.dispatch with api_key=None when the non-Bao env key is missing. SDK dispatch treats any missing key as AUTH and does not dispatch. Harmless for keyless local (explicit skip), but asymmetric for openrouter/local keyed non-Bao misses.

none: Both SDK and OpenAI-compatible call sites now resolve via principal_id+vendor_id; keyless local endpoints skip Bao lookup entirely under BAO_ADDR; CLI tier never enters the resolver path; openbao_role_id is removed from adapters and direct/API config shapes.
none: Package scope is clean — bb77ca4d..96827d55 only touches write_allow paths for wp-dispatch (api_key_resolver.py, review_dispatcher.py, their tests, and tasks.md).
